routes.question: Can all rank-10 linear extensions of a tractable full-rank 10-vertex core be proved to have at most 62 pairwise-distinct nonzero columns?
premises: A contains a nonsingular principal 10 by 10 submatrix B
extension columns v satisfy v^T B^{-1}v=0
routes.method: exact isotropic-column compatibility graph plus structural clique bound
evidence: Five standard order-62 members were constructed and exactly verified; each has no reduced rank-preserving one-vertex extension after exhaustive enumeration of all 1024 binary core columns.
Independent exact theorems now close every connected nonsingular ten-vertex core with 9, 10, or 11 edges (tree, unicyclic, bicyclic).
routes.next_test: if explicitly resumed, extend the classification to connected tricyclic ten-vertex cores

routes.question: Can a modular, orbit, or signed low-rank construction produce at least 63 distinct nonzero adjacency rows of real rank 10?
routes.method: canonical structured generation, exact modular rank filters, then rational/integer rank certification
evidence: Exact order-62 rank-10 baseline reproduced with a determinant -1 principal core and a 3844-entry rational factorization check.
All five standard extremal family members are one-vertex maximal within rank 10.
All 657 connected unicyclic ten-vertex cores have been classified; 136 are nonsingular and every exact target-53 decision is negative under two implementations.
All 2678 connected bicyclic ten-vertex cores have been classified; 719 are nonsingular and every exact target-53 decision is negative under two implementations.
routes.next_test: if explicitly resumed, search connected nonsingular tricyclic and structured denser cores for a 53-profile clique
